podcast.title: Driving and Bomb Scare Incidents (2015)
podcast.body: In 2015, Wes Scantlin was involved in a drunken police chase, reaching speeds exceeding 100 miles per hour, and received another DUI that summer. In a bizarre incident, neighbors contacted the police, believing they observed him placing a bomb in his car. Although the device was ultimately revealed to be fake, it was sufficiently convincing to prompt the deployment of a bomb squad and the evacuation of four nearby buildings. "Neighbors called the cops when they thought they spotted him putting a bomb in his car."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Airport and Airline Incidents
podcast.body: Wes Scantlin has a notorious record of problematic behavior at airports and on airlines. On September 4, 2012, a dispute with a flight attendant over alcohol on an American Airlines flight from Boston to LA led to an emergency landing in Austin, Texas, where he was arrested. In early 2015, at Denver International Airport, he rode a baggage carousel into a restricted area. Later that same year, he was arrested for disorderly conduct at Milwaukee airport. In 2016, he was denied boarding a flight to Louisville, Kentucky, due to extreme intoxication. In 2017, he was arrested at LAX for attempting to board a flight with a BB gun and has since been banned from the airport unless traveling for work. "West has a thing for getting in trouble with airlines and airports."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Escaped New Metal Classification
podcast.body: Puddle of Mud was initially categorized under the heading of new metal but eventually escaped that classification, a goal many bands fought hard to achieve. "Puddle of Mud... Most eventually escaped that classification, something that many fought very hard to do."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Legal and Financial Troubles
podcast.body: Wes Scantlin, the leader of Puddle of Mudd, has a consistent history of legal and financial difficulties. These include multiple charges of domestic violence, a ban from Graceland after diving into Elvis Presley's swimming pool, and a charge of cocaine possession. He also faced arrest for vandalism after using a circular saw on a neighbor's patio and a sledgehammer on a brick wall following a dispute. The IRS pursued him for unpaid taxes, American Express for unpaid credit card bills, and his house was foreclosed by the bank due to overdue mortgage payments, after which he illegally returned to destroy property inside. "Wes Scotland, the leader of Puddle of Mud, seems to lose an unregular basis."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Grunge Example
podcast.body: Puddle of Mudd was mentioned as a Post-Grunge band, contributing to the hybrid sound that emerged after Grunge, characterized by slicker production and more pronounced pop sensibilities. "But let's not forget about bands like Puddle of Mud and Silverchair and Live."
